newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom ends cash payment of phone bills.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom ends cash payment of phone bills.

text.p: Partly-privatised Deutsche Telekom AG said on Monday it would phase out cash-payment of telephone bills at post offices, a service which had cost over 100 million marks a year.
Recipients of welfare benefits will continue to be able to pay in cash, but others will have to switch over to paying their phone bills by direct debit or bank transfer.

Around 32 million of Telekom's customers now pay by direct debit, with a further 7.5 million making monthly transfers. The remaining 1.4 million pay cash -- at a cost to the company of up to seven marks a time, the company said in a statement.
